exposure: COVID-19 infection on the day of delivery
outcome: placental histopathological changes (intravillous fetal thrombosis, fibrin deposition, lymphocytic infiltration, chorangiosis, edema, intervillous hemorrhage, syncytial node formation, distal villous hypoplasia, avascular villi)
cohort: The study included 40 pregnant women referred to Ganjavian hospital for delivery, divided into groups with and without COVID-19 infection on the day of delivery.
finding: Pregnant women infected with COVID-19 during their third trimester showed significantly higher rates of various placental abnormalities compared to uninfected women, indicating tissue changes that can lead to poor maternal-fetal exchange.
mod_finding: No significant differences were found between COVID-19 infected and uninfected groups regarding the mode of delivery.
cross-section timing: Data collected from June-October 2021 at the time of delivery.
